- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use 14-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag; add 1-2 day buffer to forecast direction.
